free.title: FEAST OF SAN GENNARO
free.caption:
FREE · LITTLE ITALY

100 years ago, Neapolitan immigrants threw a one-day block party for their patron saint on Mulberry Street. This year the Feast of San Gennaro turns 100, and it's still free to walk.

Sept 17-27, 300+ vendors line Mulberry, Hester and Grand streets under string lights for zeppole, sausage and peppers, and cannoli-eating contests. On Sept 19, the Grand Procession carries San Gennaro's statue down Mulberry after Mass at Most Precious Blood Church.

Go on a weekday afternoon if you actually want to walk - Friday and Saturday nights get packed shoulder to shoulder.

Tag whoever still owes you a slice.

food.title: MURRAY'S CHEESE
food.caption:
FOOD & MARKET · GREENWICH VILLAGE

Murray's Cheese has been running the cheese counter on Bleecker Street since 1962 - 64 years of cheesemongers who'll cut you a taste before you buy anything.

Walk in any day 9AM-8PM for the Mac & Cheese counter (melts from $9), grab-and-go cheese boards for a park picnic, or just ask a cheesemonger to walk you through what's good that week. Hundreds of cheeses, charcuterie, and cheese classes run upstairs if you want to go deeper.

Ask before you buy - sampling is the whole point of shopping here, and the mongers behind the counter expect it.

Send this to whoever's hosting the next cheese board night.

art.title: 6 SECRETS OF THE CHRYSLER BUILDING
art.caption:
HIDDEN GEM · MIDTOWN EAST

The Chrysler Building's spire was built in total secret - assembled inside the frame and hoisted into place in 90 minutes on October 23, 1929, just to beat a rival tower to the title of world's tallest building.

The lobby is free to walk into on weekdays, 8AM to 6PM. Look up at the 110-by-67-foot ceiling mural, the 32 elevator cabs with different wood doors, and the 61st-floor eagle gargoyles - giant replicas of a 1929 Chrysler hood ornament. The old observation deck cost 50 cents, until the Empire State Building took its business in 1945.

No ticket, no line, just walk in like you own the place.

Send this to whoever thinks they've seen everything in Midtown.
